is_anopheles.evidence: The study identifies Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus as the primary vectors (Abstract, Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports on the frequency of knock down resistance (kdr) genotypes (Abstract, Page 1; Table 3, Page 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 3 on page 6 provides genotype counts (kdrRR, kdrR/S, kdrSS) for Anopheles gambiae s.s. in both wet and dry seasons.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in the Kintampo North and South districts of Ghana (Methods, Page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary entomological study describing field collections and subsequent laboratory analysis (Abstract, Page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported for the Kintampo area, with specific community names provided in Table 2 (e.g., Ajina, Asantekwa, Ntereban) (Page 6).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted from November 2003 to November 2005 (Abstract, Page 1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study was conducted by the Kintampo Health Research Centre as part of preparation for drug and vaccine trials; while it uses a known surveillance system (KHDSS), the specific genotype data appears unique to this report.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and location information are contained within the main text and tables of the provided PDF.

assessment.summary: This study characterizes malaria transmission and vector populations in the forest-savannah transitional zone of Kintampo, Ghana, between 2003 and 2005. It identifies Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles funestus as the main vectors and provides kdr (Vgsc L995F) genotype counts for a subset of An. gambiae s.s. mosquitoes collected during the wet and dry seasons.
